parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit has one file, order-item.entity.ts. Its concern is cohesive: one OrderItem value object. However, it checks the same order-item rules in two places. In `addValidators()` it registers the library's validator objects (OrderItemQuantityValidator, OrderItemProductValidator, OrderItemPriceValidator). It also has its own private static checks, `validateQuantity` and `validateProductName`, which `create()` calls directly and which throw BrokenRulesException. Those checks skip the validator mechanism the class itself registers. The quantity rule is also run twice on one path: `withQuantity` calls `OrderItem.validateQuantity(newQuantity)` and then `OrderItem.create(...)`, which runs it again. The increment rule in `withIncreasedQuantity` is a third inline check. The class names strongly suggest the validators enforce the same quantity and product rules, so the invariant does not live in one place. I couldn't see the validator source, which is why confidence is moderate. There is also a smaller inconsistency: the file is named `*.entity.ts` and sits under entities/, but the class extends DddValueObject and its doc calls it a value object. The doc example also uses `changeQuantity`, which doesn't exist; the method is `withQuantity`.

violations.message: The quantity and product-name rules are checked twice. The private static `validateQuantity` and `validateProductName`, called from `create`, run outside the validator mechanism. The same rules also appear to be in OrderItemQuantityValidator and OrderItemProductValidator, which `addValidators()` registers. Keep these rules in one place.
`withQuantity` calls `validateQuantity` and then `create`, which checks quantity again, so the rule runs twice on the same path.
